newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to buy U.S. pork bellies until late May.
newsitem.headline: Japan to buy U.S. pork bellies until late May.

text.p: Japanese trade houses said on Thursday they would continue to buy U.S. pork bellies until late May in order to cover requirements for the rest of the year.
On Wednesday, rumours that Japan was buying light-weight U.S. pork bellies boosted Chicago pork belly futures to their highest levels since last August.

"After the Japanese government imposed an import ban on all Taiwanese pork, we had to look for alternative sources," said a senior official of a major trade house. "At the moment the U.S. is the most reliable supplier."
Another trade house official said: "We've covered pork bellies until August shipments, but as Taiwanese pork is not available, we'd like to cover our requirements for this year by the end of May."

Although Taiwan said earlier on Thursday it had lifted the export ban on pork it had imposed on March 20 due to an outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease, Japan's Agriculture Ministry said it will maintain its ban indefinitely.
Japan is the largest export market for Taiwanese pork. About 40 percent of the total 653,176 tonnes Japan imported in 1996 came from Taiwan, the Finance Ministry said.
Of the total pork imports, pork bellies accounted for 170,000 to 180,000 tonnes, industry officials said.
Local traders said U.S. pork exporters are intentionally raising offer prices to Japan.

"This is a typical seller's market. They know that we have no other alternative suppliers. Some exporters have raised offer prices by as much as 25 percent against a year earlier," a third trade house official said. -- Eiichiro Tokumoto, Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7391
